summary.text: Spearman Mulius, son-in-law of Augeias and husband of fair-haired Agamede, whom Nestor slew in the old war between the Pylians and the Epeians — distinct from `mulius-trojan` whom Patroclus killed and from `mulius-iliad20` whom Achilles smote at Troy.

story.text: When the strife of the Pylians and Epeians began, Nestor was first to slay his man and win single-hooved horses — even the spearman Mulius, son by marriage of Augeias, who had to wife his eldest daughter fair-haired Agamede, who knew all simples that the wide earth nourisheth. Him as he came against Nestor the old king smote with his bronze-tipped spear, and he fell in the dust.
